content.text:
---
title: Web App Files
description: How the Files browser, mounted drives, metadata index, and reusable previews work.
---

# Web App Files

The `/files` browser presents one user-wide library across mounted drives.
Genesis keeps provider-neutral metadata in Postgres and keeps file bytes in
their owning drive.

## Files Browser

`/files` is the user-wide file browser. Places such as All files, Recent, and
Trash aggregate metadata across drives. Selecting a drive entry limits the
library to that mount.

External storage appears as separate, bounded provider hierarchies rather than
a flat corpus. Box mounts one connected account per user and refreshes folders
from Box as they are opened. In sessions, explicitly attached Box files are read
first; otherwise Genesis searches and fetches through the Box Files mount before
falling back to hosted Box MCP for unavailable/missing results, Box AI, or
collaboration operations. Each connected personal Google account has its own
Google My Drive entry.
Each active Workspace connection has its own domain entry containing the
current user's My Drive and the Shared Drives that user may access. Personal
accounts and Workspace domains do not share credentials or merge corpora.

The UI and API treat files as indexed provider objects, not opaque blobs in
Postgres. A `file_drive` row describes each mount. A `drive_file` row stores its
scope, hierarchy, provider locator, lifecycle state, fingerprint, and display
metadata. It never stores file bytes.

| Route / API | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/files` | Browse, search, filter, preview, and manage files across mounted drives. |
| `GET /api/drive-files/drives` | List already-provisioned mounts and indexed metadata by place, drive, folder, type, and lifecycle state. |
| `GET /api/drive-files/:id/content` | Stream authorized bytes from the owning provider. |
| `POST /api/drive-files/files` | Create a supported file in the selected writable drive and folder. |
| `POST /api/drive-files/uploads/prepare` | Authorize one file and return a short-lived direct-upload destination. |
| `POST /api/drive-files/uploads/finalize` | Verify and index a completed direct upload. |
| `POST /api/drive-files/upload` | Legacy server-relayed upload path during the transition. |
| `/api/drive-files/*` mutations | Create folders; rename, move, trash, restore, or permanently delete provider objects. |

All files and Recent are flat file-only views across mounts. They exclude
folders so a child appears once without also presenting a partial cross-drive
folder tree. Selecting a drive restores its folder hierarchy and the Folders
filter. Folder selection is scoped to one drive because provider hierarchies do
not cross drive boundaries.
The browser keeps the complete authorized metadata corpus in its
permission-scoped IndexedDB index so aggregate counts, search, and folder
navigation do not depend on the currently rendered viewport. The list and grid
virtualize their rows and only mount visible content plus a small overscan
window. Drive views are folder-first and naturally sorted by name. Recent sorts
files by most recently modified, with stable name and file-ID tie-breakers.

The title-bar New menu follows the selected location. Genesis creates Markdown
files. Writable Workspace mounts create native Docs, Sheets, and Slides.
Personal Google My Drive mounts use **Add from Google** and do not show New or
filesystem Upload actions. New files receive an available untitled name, appear
in the metadata index immediately, and open in the standard preview sidebar.
Genesis presentation creation stays in its builder until presentation records
have stable Files identity.

When the aggregate library is genuinely empty, `/files` offers an upload action
and a link to `/files/help`. The help page explains Genesis and Google Drive in
the current drive model and can upload the first file directly into Genesis.
Loading, indexing, provider failures, empty folders, and filtered-empty results
remain separate states.

File previews use a unified **preview kind registry**
(`file-preview-registry.tsx`, `file-preview-kinds.tsx`). Images, PDFs, text,
Office files, and other kinds map to shared renderers. Unsupported formats
provide a clear open-file fallback.

Preview content is independent of placement:

- `/files` pins previews into URL-backed tabs in the app shell sidebar;
- pages that need more room can use `DriveFilePreviewSheet`, the standard wide
  slide-over host;
- builder and app-shell surfaces can use `FilePreviewFlyout`, a resizable
  portal-hosted panel that keeps preview errors isolated from shell registration
  (#991);
- session composer chips and transcript attachment clicks open
  `AttachmentFilePreview` → `FilesPreviewSheet` with the same preview kind
  registry (`attachment-file-preview.tsx`, #1189);
- all hosts share preview, details, loading, failure, open, download, and delete
  behavior through `DriveFilePreviewSurface`.

The owning page chooses the host. File-type components must not depend on the
Files route or assume that every preview is a sheet.

Gallery specimens for the renderer, pinned panel, slide-over, and flyout live at
`/dev/ui/file-preview`.

The multi-drive library and picker specimen lives at `/dev/ui/file-browser`,
including multiple personal Google accounts, Workspace domains, and Box.

Genesis Drive is the built-in mount backed by the organization's tenant S3
bucket. Personal objects use versioned, user-scoped object keys. Folder
navigation is URL-backed and uses metadata-backed containers and breadcrumbs.
Users can create folders, upload, rename, move, select multiple items, and apply
bulk actions.

Files can be dropped onto the open center pane or onto a writable drive row in
the sidebar. The center target uses the selected drive and current folder; a
sidebar target always uses that drive's root. A browser worker batches multiple
files with bounded concurrency, retries explicit transient failures, keeps a
cancellable progress toast visible, and continues while the user browses other
folders. Google My Drive is not a drop target because its `drive.file` mount is
Picker-only.

File bytes do not normally relay through the web API. For Genesis Drive, the
prepare route returns a ten-minute, object-specific S3 PUT URL with a signed
create-only condition and required headers. For Google Workspace Drive, the
server uses its delegated credential to create a file-scoped resumable upload
session, then returns only that session URI; the OAuth access token stays
server-side. Providers without a safe browser upload session, currently Box,
use the bounded API relay strategy so the bearer token never enters the
browser. The worker uploads to the selected provider, and the server writes the
provider-neutral index row and publishes Files invalidation. Cancellation
aborts active network requests and skips queued files.

Tenant object-storage provisioning applies the browser CORS policy before an
organization becomes active. It allows browser origins and request headers so
local development, PR previews, and deployed hosts can use presigned requests
without enumerating every origin. This does not make the bucket public: every
read or write still requires an object-specific, short-lived signed URL. Buckets
created before this provisioning behavior are repaired at app startup and,
temporarily, again on their first direct upload. The lazy repair can be removed
after existing tenant buckets have received the policy.

The wildcard CORS origin is a deliberate v1 transport decision, not an
authorization grant. Browser requests do not carry bucket cookies or ambient
credentials; possession of the ten-minute, object-specific signed URL is the
only authority, and Genesis signs create-only uploads with required headers.
The accepted residual risk is that a leaked URL can be used from any origin
until it expires. This supports unknown PR-preview hosts and must be revisited
if uploads gain longer-lived URLs, overwrite authority, or browser credentials.

Moving an item to Trash changes its indexed lifecycle state without deleting its
bytes. Restore returns the item and, when necessary, restores its parent folder
chain. From Trash, a user can permanently delete one or more items after an
irreversible-action confirmation. Permanent deletion removes the scoped Genesis
Drive objects before deleting their metadata rows.

In the file list, rows with `source: generated` (session PDFs, images, and
other agent-written outputs) show the Genesis brand gradient on the file icon.
User uploads (`uploaded`) and provider references use the standard muted icon.
Folder navigation uses a breadcrumb in the list header — current folder is plain
text; only parent segments are links back up the tree.

## Drives and Providers

Low-level provider behavior lives behind `FileProviderAdapter` in
`apps/web/src/services/file-providers/`. Mounted external drives register a
driver in `src/services/mounted-cloud-drive-drivers/`; the driver selects the
adapter, resolves mount-specific authority, chooses indexed or lazy listing,
and owns disconnect/access-loss behavior. Shared metadata normalization lives
in `mounted-cloud-drive-file-index.ts`. The web layer maps provider ids to
labels and external URLs in `src/web/lib/file-providers.ts`.

| Drive | Role today |
| --- | --- |
| Genesis | Built in for every provisioned organization. My Drive uses the current user's S3 scope; Company Drive uses organization scope and is shared with organization members who have Files access. Both store bytes in the same tenant S3 bucket. |
| Google My Drive | The Google login account is mounted automatically after the org-scoped consent grant. Users may connect additional accounts through Genesis Google OAuth (`auth.agentcompany.com`). Multiple accounts per user are supported. Existing content is added only through the **native Google File Picker**. |
| Google Workspace Drive | Org admin connects one or more service accounts (domain-wide delegation). After verify + activate, each user sees only My Drive and Shared Drives they can access under that domain. |
| Box | User connects through brokered Box OAuth. The mount lists and indexes each folder on demand, streams provider bytes through the authorized content route, and supports the capabilities declared by the mount. |

The Files sidebar lists Genesis (My Drive + Company Drive), each personal Google
My Drive account, and each Workspace domain (My Drive + shared drives under that
connection). Company Drive means organization-wide Genesis storage in this phase;
it is not a separate drive for every Agentic Team.

Adding a mounted provider means a server adapter, mounted cloud-drive driver,
mount lifecycle, schema kind, attachment/provider types, and Files UI grouping.
The repository agent checklist is
`.agents/skills/genesis-integration/references/file-storage-integrations.md`.
Do not hardcode provider assumptions in shared CRUD/content routes or define
Genesis as "anything that is not Google." The metadata contract and preview
registry remain provider-neutral.

## Google indexing and setup

- **Google My Drive** never full-crawls. Only Picker-selected (and nested
  expanded / app-created) items appear.
- The Google login account is mounted idempotently after org-scoped consent.
  Disconnecting it records durable user intent so later logins do not restore
  it. Explicitly connecting that account again clears the marker. Repeated
  connect attempts converge on the existing account and mount.
- **Google Workspace Drive** mounts appear after an org connection is
  **active**. Periodic organization reconciliation ensures permission-aware
  mounts for every active organization member, independent of whether they
  open Files. Opening `/files` remains an idempotent recovery path for the
  current user; it does not run a whole-drive sync.
- Each Workspace mount and index belongs to one user and is built with that
  user's delegated Google identity. Shared metadata is never used to grant
  another organization member access.
- Disconnecting a Workspace entry removes that user's mounts and index while
  retaining the organization connection for other users. Automatic Files
  reconciliation respects that choice; an explicit setup or recovery flow
  re-provisions the signed-in user's mounts and reconnects them later.
- Membership and Shared Drive changes are reconciled in the background. A
  removed organization member's Workspace mounts and indexed metadata are
  purged. Google removal events hide the affected folder tree so descendants
  cannot remain visible after access is lost.
- Workspace connection lifecycle audit reads are organization-scoped. Legacy
  audit rows without an organization id are intentionally unavailable because
  their tenant ownership cannot be reconstructed safely.
- Interim app-process index and repair periodic jobs run globally by default,
  but process only active Workspace connections. `GENESIS_GOOGLE_DRIVE_INDEX_DISABLED=1`
  stops indexing and Workspace membership/mount reconciliation;
  `GENESIS_GOOGLE_DRIVE_REPAIR_DISABLED=1` independently stops repair. GFD-309
  moves these jobs to a dedicated organization task processor.
- Workspace setup is available from Add cloud drive. Production readiness is
  tracked in the
  [Google File Drives rollout review](../../plans/google-file-drives-rollout-review.md).

Committed metadata and mount changes invalidate authorized Files clients over
the app WebSocket. Each active client performs an authoritative refresh and
reconciles its IndexedDB snapshots, including removing drives and files the
server no longer returns. Reconnect and manual refresh use the same
reconciliation path.

## Boundaries

Indexed metadata and preview access are not hidden authority.

The current user and organization scope are checked on every Files API path.
Provider credentials remain in the integration layer. Permanent deletion still
requires explicit confirmation; indexing never expands provider permissions or
copies provider bytes into Postgres. Workspace reads and mutations use the
current mount owner's delegated token; there is no organization-admin token
fallback for file access.

| Box | User connects through brokered Box OAuth. The mount lists and indexes each folder on demand, streams provider bytes through the authorized content route, and supports the capabilities declared by the mount. |
| Dropbox | User connects through brokered Dropbox OAuth. or Dropbox account, each personal Google My Drive account, and each Workspace
domain (My Drive + shared drives under that connection). Company Drive means
organization-wide Genesis storage in this phase;

content.thinking:
**Evaluating delete actions**

Routes require a distinction between `trash` for temporary actions and `delete` for permanent removal. The delete action is only available for files in the Trash, but I wonder if the “file storage” requirement should include delete functionality too. I think mapping Dropbox's delete_v2 to `trashFile` makes sense; restoring files entails using `files/restore` with specific parameters. There's a complex interplay here, especially since our adapter may not support certain metadata needs for restore. Dropbox's deletion is soft, allowing recovery, but our current setup complicates restoration.

**Evaluating delete capabilities**

I’m thinking that choosing no trash and no delete capability means users cannot delete anything. However, the adapter does require a delete function, which is a bit confusing. Perhaps I could add a `"delete"` option and make that accessible in the UI for truly permanent deletions of active items. I'll need to check what actions are allowed, as the delete function might only apply to files in the Trash, based on my earlier notes.

---
name: dropbox
description: Use Dropbox for files, folders, search, sharing, file requests, and revisions.
---

# Dropbox

Use this capability when the user's task involves Dropbox content, organization,
sharing, file requests, or revision history.

For file discovery and reading, use this order:

1. If the user attached a Dropbox file, inspect the workspace attachment first.
2. For inventory, root listing, or folder browsing, call `mounted_drive_list`
   with `provider: "dropbox"`. Omit `folderId` for the root. To descend, pass
   the returned `driveId`. Pass the folder's `providerObjectId` as `folderId`.
3. For named or topical discovery, call `mounted_drive_search` with
   `provider: "dropbox"`.
4. Call `mounted_drive_fetch` for the selected file result.
5. Fall back to Dropbox MCP when the mounted drive is unavailable, returns no
   match, or cannot fetch the file. Use MCP for shared links, file requests,
   revisions, transcription, and document-to-Markdown conversion.

For MCP fallback, call `mcp_list_tools` with slug `dropbox`, then use
`mcp_call_tool` with a returned tool name. Do not hardcode remote tool names.
Do not pass the registry id `connection:dropbox` as the MCP slug.

Keep access within the user's existing Dropbox permissions. Ask before actions
that create, change, move, delete, share, restore, or request content.

If Dropbox access is unavailable, tell the user to connect Dropbox in Genesis
Settings. If connection registration fails, explain that Dropbox must approve
Genesis as a trusted DCR client.

-- Check constraints are not rewritten by additive drift when their definition
-- changes. Keep the mounted-provider kind/account rules aligned with the
-- declarative schema, and preserve personal plus organization Genesis drives.
--
-- Repeatables run before greenfield schema bootstrap, so this must be a no-op
-- until the declarative schema has created file_drive.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF to_regclass('public.file_drive') IS NULL THEN
    RETURN;
  END IF;

  -- The declarative schema replaces this legacy org-only uniqueness constraint
  -- with one Genesis mount per owner scope.
  DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.uidx_file_drive_genesis_org;

  -- Keep only the most recently updated Box mount active for each user before
  -- enforcing the single-active-account invariant on existing databases.
  WITH ranked_box_mounts AS (
    SELECT
      id,
      row_number() OVER (
        PARTITION BY org_id, owner_scope_type, owner_scope_id
        ORDER BY updated_at DESC, created_at DESC, id DESC
      ) AS active_rank
    FROM public.file_drive
    WHERE kind = 'box' AND status != 'disconnected'
  )
  UPDATE public.file_drive AS drive
  SET status = 'disconnected', updated_at = now()
  FROM ranked_box_mounts AS ranked
  WHERE drive.id = ranked.id AND ranked.active_rank > 1;

  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uidx_file_drive_box_active_owner
    ON public.file_drive (org_id, owner_scope_type, owner_scope_id)
    WHERE kind = 'box' AND status != 'disconnected';

  -- Apply the same single-active-account rule to Dropbox mounts.
  WITH ranked_dropbox_mounts AS (
    SELECT
      id,
      row_number() OVER (
        PARTITION BY org_id, owner_scope_type, owner_scope_id
        ORDER BY updated_at DESC, created_at DESC, id DESC
      ) AS active_rank
    FROM public.file_drive
    WHERE kind = 'dropbox' AND status != 'disconnected'
  )
  UPDATE public.file_drive AS drive
  SET status = 'disconnected', updated_at = now()
  FROM ranked_dropbox_mounts AS ranked
  WHERE drive.id = ranked.id AND ranked.active_rank > 1;

  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uidx_file_drive_dropbox_active_owner
    ON public.file_drive (org_id, owner_scope_type, owner_scope_id)
    WHERE kind = 'dropbox' AND status != 'disconnected';

  -- Box REST search backs mounted-drive-first discovery in sessions. Keep
  -- mounts created before that capability shipped aligned without reconnecting.
  UPDATE public.file_drive
  SET capabilities = capabilities || '["search"]'::jsonb, updated_at = now()
  WHERE kind = 'box' AND NOT (capabilities ? 'search');

  -- Check constraints are named objects, so additive schema drift cannot
  -- widen them when a new mounted provider kind is introduced.
  ALTER TABLE public.file_drive
    DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS chk_file_drive_kind,
    DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS chk_file_drive_google_connection,
    DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS chk_file_drive_genesis_owner;

  ALTER TABLE public.file_drive
    ADD CONSTRAINT chk_file_drive_kind
    CHECK (
      kind IN (
        'genesis_s3',
        'google_drive',
        'google_my_drive',
        'google_workspace_drive',
        'box',
        'dropbox'
      )
    ),
    ADD CONSTRAINT chk_file_drive_google_connection
    CHECK (
      kind NOT IN ('google_drive', 'google_my_drive', 'google_workspace_drive', 'box', 'dropbox')
      OR (
        owner_scope_type = 'user'
        AND connection_id IS NOT NULL
        AND provider_account_id IS NOT NULL
      )
    ),
    ADD CONSTRAINT chk_file_drive_genesis_owner
    CHECK (
      kind != 'genesis_s3'
      OR (
        connection_id IS NULL
        AND provider_account_id IS NULL
        AND (
          owner_scope_type = 'user'
          OR (owner_scope_type = 'org' AND owner_scope_id = org_id)
        )
      )
    );
END $$;

/**
 * Drizzle schema: files domain.
 */

import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import {
  bigint,
  check,
  index,
  jsonb,
  pgTable,
  text,
  timestamp,
  uniqueIndex,
} from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import { appUser } from "./core";

/**
 * Next-generation mounted storage service.
 *
 * This is additive while the legacy file_reference routes remain live. The
 * controlled Files and Drives cutover will rebuild the index into drive_file
 * and then remove the legacy shape.
 */
export const fileDrive = pgTable(
  "file_drive",
  {
    id: text("id")
      .primaryKey()
      .$defaultFn(() => crypto.randomUUID()),
    orgId: text("org_id").notNull(),
    kind: text("kind").notNull(),
    displayName: text("display_name").notNull(),
    connectionId: text("connection_id"),
    ownerScopeType: text("owner_scope_type").notNull(),
    ownerScopeId: text("owner_scope_id").notNull(),
    providerAccountId: text("provider_account_id"),
    providerRootId: text("provider_root_id"),
    status: text("status").notNull().default("active"),
    capabilities: jsonb("capabilities").$type<string[]>().notNull().default([]),
    syncCursor: text("sync_cursor"),
    lastSyncedAt: timestamp("last_synced_at"),
    lastErrorCode: text("last_error_code"),
    createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
    updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
  },
  (t) => [
    index("idx_file_drive_org_owner").on(t.orgId, t.ownerScopeType, t.ownerScopeId),
    uniqueIndex("uidx_file_drive_org_kind_owner_account").on(
      t.orgId,
      t.kind,
      t.ownerScopeType,
      t.ownerScopeId,
      t.providerAccountId,
    ),
    uniqueIndex("uidx_file_drive_genesis_owner")
      .on(t.orgId, t.ownerScopeType, t.ownerScopeId)
      .where(sql`${t.kind} = 'genesis_s3'`),
    uniqueIndex("uidx_file_drive_box_active_owner")
      .on(t.orgId, t.ownerScopeType, t.ownerScopeId)
      .where(sql`${t.kind} = 'box' and ${t.status} != 'disconnected'`),
    uniqueIndex("uidx_file_drive_dropbox_active_owner")
      .on(t.orgId, t.ownerScopeType, t.ownerScopeId)
      .where(sql`${t.kind} = 'dropbox' and ${t.status} != 'disconnected'`),
    check(
      "chk_file_drive_kind",
      sql`${t.kind} in ('genesis_s3', 'google_drive', 'google_my_drive', 'google_workspace_drive', 'box', 'dropbox')`,
    ),
    check("chk_file_drive_owner_scope", sql`${t.ownerScopeType} in ('user', 'org')`),
    check(
      "chk_file_drive_genesis_owner",
      sql`${t.kind} != 'genesis_s3' or (
        ${t.connectionId} is null
        and ${t.providerAccountId} is null
        and (
          ${t.ownerScopeType} = 'user'
          or (${t.ownerScopeType} = 'org' and ${t.ownerScopeId} = ${t.orgId})
        )
      )`,
    ),
    check(
      "chk_file_drive_google_connection",
      sql`${t.kind} not in ('google_drive', 'google_my_drive', 'google_workspace_drive', 'box', 'dropbox')
        or (${t.ownerScopeType} = 'user' and ${t.connectionId} is not null and ${t.providerAccountId} is not null)`,
    ),
    check(
      "chk_file_drive_status",
      sql`${t.status} in ('active', 'syncing', 'reauth_required', 'unavailable', 'disconnected')`,
    ),
  ],
);

/**
 * Per-account Google My Drive OAuth credentials (drive.file + identity).
 * Separate from login Google identity and Gmail/Calendar Workspace grants.
 */
export const googleMyDriveAccount = pgTable(
  "google_my_drive_account",
  {
    id: text("id")
      .primaryKey()
      .$defaultFn(() => crypto.randomUUID()),
    orgId: text("org_id").notNull(),
    userId: text("user_id")
      .notNull()
      .references(() => appUser.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    googleSub: text("google_sub").notNull(),
    email: text("email").notNull(),
    encryptedRefreshToken: text("encrypted_refresh_token"),
    encryptedAccessToken: text("encrypted_access_token"),
    accessTokenExpiresAt: timestamp("access_token_expires_at"),
    scopes: text("scopes"),
    status: text("status").notNull().default("active"),
    lastErrorCode: text("last_error_code"),
    createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
    updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
  },
  (t) => [
    uniqueIndex("uidx_google_my_drive_account_org_user_sub").on(t.orgId, t.userId, t.googleSub),
    index("idx_google_my_drive_account_org_user").on(t.orgId, t.userId),
    check(
      "chk_google_my_drive_account_status",
      sql`${t.status} in ('active', 'reauth_required', 'disconnected')`,
    ),
  ],
);

/**
 * Provider-neutral file metadata index. File bytes never live in this table.
 */
export const driveFile = pgTable(
  "drive_file",
  {
    id: text("id")
      .primaryKey()
      .$defaultFn(() => crypto.randomUUID()),
    orgId: text("org_id").notNull(),
    driveId: text("drive_id")
      .notNull()
      .references(() => fileDrive.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    scopeType: text("scope_type").notNull(),
    scopeId: text("scope_id").notNull(),
    parentId: text("parent_id"),
    name: text("name").notNull(),
    kind: text("kind").notNull(),
    mimeType: text("mime_type"),
    sizeBytes: bigint("size_bytes", { mode: "number" }),
    locatorKind: text("locator_kind").notNull(),
    objectKey: text("object_key"),
    providerObjectId: text("provider_object_id"),
    referenceKind: text("reference_kind"),
    referenceId: text("reference_id"),
    contentVersion: text("content_version"),
    contentEtag: text("content_etag"),
    contentHash: text("content_hash"),
    metadataHash: text("metadata_hash").notNull(),
    providerCreatedAt: timestamp("provider_created_at"),
    providerModifiedAt: timestamp("provider_modified_at"),
    providerOwnerName: text("provider_owner_name"),
    providerOwnerEmail: text("provider_owner_email"),
    lastVerifiedAt: timestamp("last_verified_at"),
    status: text("status").notNull().default("active"),
    createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
    updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
  },
  (t) => [
    index("idx_drive_file_org_scope").on(t.orgId, t.scopeType, t.scopeId),
    index("idx_drive_file_drive_parent").on(t.driveId, t.parentId),
    uniqueIndex("uidx_drive_file_provider_object")
      .on(t.driveId, t.providerObjectId)
      .where(sql`${t.providerObjectId} is not null`),
    uniqueIndex("uidx_drive_file_object_key")
      .on(t.driveId, t.objectKey)
      .where(sql`${t.objectKey} is not null`),
    uniqueIndex("uidx_drive_file_native_object")
      .on(t.driveId, t.referenceKind, t.referenceId)
      .where(sql`${t.referenceKind} is not null and ${t.referenceId} is not null`),
    check("chk_drive_file_scope", sql`${t.scopeType} in ('user', 'team', 'org')`),
    check(
      "chk_drive_file_locator_kind",
      sql`${t.locatorKind} in ('s3_object', 'provider_object', 'native_object')`,
    ),
    check(
      "chk_drive_file_locator",
      sql`(
        (${t.locatorKind} = 's3_object' and ${t.objectKey} is not null and ${t.providerObjectId} is null and ${t.referenceKind} is null and ${t.referenceId} is null)
        or
        (${t.locatorKind} = 'provider_object' and ${t.objectKey} is null and ${t.providerObjectId} is not null and ${t.referenceKind} is null and ${t.referenceId} is null)
        or
        (${t.locatorKind} = 'native_object' and ${t.objectKey} is null and ${t.providerObjectId} is null and ${t.referenceKind} is not null and ${t.referenceId} is not null)
      )`,
    ),
    check(
      "chk_drive_file_status",
      sql`${t.status} in ('active', 'trashed', 'unavailable', 'sync_pending', 'conflicted')`,
    ),
    check("chk_drive_file_size", sql`${t.sizeBytes} is null or ${t.sizeBytes} >= 0`),
  ],
);

/** @deprecated Replaced by fileDrive + driveFile after the controlled cutover. */
export const fileReference = pgTable(
  "file_reference",
  {
    id: text("id")
      .primaryKey()
      .$defaultFn(() => crypto.randomUUID()),
    orgId: text("org_id").notNull(),
    userId: text("user_id")
      .notNull()
      .references(() => appUser.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    provider: text("provider").notNull(),
    providerFileId: text("provider_file_id").notNull(),
    name: text("name").notNull(),
    mimeType: text("mime_type"),
    source: text("source").notNull(),
    folderId: text("folder_id"),
    size: text("size"),
    providerCreatedAt: timestamp("provider_created_at"),
    providerModifiedAt: timestamp("provider_modified_at"),
    providerOwnerName: text("provider_owner_name"),
    providerOwnerEmail: text("provider_owner_email"),
    lastVerifiedAt: timestamp("last_verified_at"),
    status: text("status").notNull().default("active"),
    createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
  },
  (t) => [index("idx_file_reference_org_user").on(t.orgId, t.userId)],
);

---
name: genesis-product-docs
description: Use when recent product or web-app changes may have drifted docs/product or AGENTS.md, when a scheduled docs sync runs, or when adding durable product behavior that agents and developers need to find quickly. Guides review of recent commits, updates to docs/product (especially web-app pages), and small AGENTS.md learned-fact updates without duplicating plan docs.
---

# Genesis Product Docs

This skill keeps `docs/product/` aligned with shipped product behavior. It
composes with `genesis-doctrine`; it does not replace founding docs or kernel
plans.

## When To Use

- Cron or automation asks to review recent commits for doc/skill drift.
- A PR changes `apps/web` product surfaces, Hub sessions, integrations, or
  app-hosted Connections.
- An agent needs to know **what exists now** vs what plans promise later.

Skip for pure research (use `genesis-research`), kernel-only changes (kernel
product docs + `packages/hub/PROTOCOL.md`), or plan/task ledger updates only.

## Start Here

1. Read `AGENTS.md` and `docs/agent-brief.md`.
2. Load `.agents/skills/genesis-doctrine/SKILL.md` for non-trivial product edits.
3. Read `docs/writing-standard.md` and `docs/template.md` before adding pages.
4. Scan recent commits (default: last 24 hours on `main`).

# Genesis Product Docs

This skill keeps `docs/product/` aligned with shipped product behavior. It
composes with `genesis-doctrine`; it does not replace founding docs or kernel
plans.

## When To Use

- Cron or automation asks to review recent commits for doc/skill drift.
- A PR changes `apps/web` product surfaces, Hub sessions, integrations, or
  app-hosted Connections.
- An agent needs to know **what exists now** vs what plans promise later.

Skip for pure research (use `genesis-research`), kernel-only changes (kernel
product docs + `packages/hub/PROTOCOL.md`), or plan/task ledger updates only.

## Start Here

1. Read `AGENTS.md` and `docs/agent-brief.md`.
2. Load `.agents/skills/genesis-doctrine/SKILL.md` for non-trivial product edits.
3. Read `docs/writing-standard.md` and `docs/template.md` before adding pages.
4. Scan recent commits (default: last 24 hours on `main`).

---
title: Writing Standard
description: The rules for writing and extending Genesis founding docs.
---

# Writing Standard

This standard keeps Genesis docs consistent as more contributors and agents add material.

## Read Order

Before creating or changing a founding doc, read:

1. `PRODUCT.md`
2. `DESIGN.md`
3. This standard
4. `docs/template.md`

## Invariants

1. GitHub is the base interface. Markdown must stand on its own.
2. One page, one primary idea.
3. Every page has one visible `#` heading.
4. Section headings name the concept directly.
5. Claims must help a contributor make a better product, architecture, or implementation decision.
6. Prefer concrete doctrine over inspirational language.
7. Avoid market-size framing, investor language, and launch rhetoric.
8. Avoid generic AI SaaS phrasing.
9. Use diagrams only when they reduce ambiguity.
10. Static HTML may improve reading, but it must not become the only way to understand the page.
11. Use the illustration standard in `DESIGN.md` for diagrams and generated visuals.
12. Highlight first-use doctrine terms only when they are expanded elsewhere.

## Page Shape

Use this order unless the page has a clear reason to differ:

1. Frontmatter with `title` and `description`.
2. One `#` heading matching the durable page name.
3. A short opening paragraph that states the page's purpose.
4. Named sections with `##` headings.
5. Short paragraphs, lists, or tables that make the standard actionable.
6. Optional open questions or editing notes at the end.

## Voice

Genesis writing should be exacting, premium, and practical.

Use:

- Short doctrine.
- Working definitions.
- Specific product language.
- Concrete constraints.
- Plain statements that can be argued with.

Avoid:

- Pitch-deck language.
- Enterprise transformation language.
- Motivational filler.
- Future-tense grandeur.
- Abstract principles that cannot change a decision.

## Visual Standard

The rendered site should feel like a composed operating manual, not a landing page.

- Use warm paper, warm ink, and sparse Genesis Gold.
- Keep prose readable at 65 to 75 characters where layout allows.
- Use full borders for callouts. Do not use thick side-stripe accents.
- Do not use gradient text.
- Do not use decorative glassmorphism.
- Keep the docs navigation to one primary header menu.
- Fenced `mermaid` blocks render on the VitePress site via
  `v-beautiful-mermaid`. GitHub still shows the source; keep a short prose
  summary when the diagram carries essential structure (plans and architecture
  pages).

## Agent Workflow

When an agent edits docs:

1. Read the project context and this standard.
2. Decide whether the change is content, structure, visual style, or tooling.
3. Keep the edit in the smallest relevant file set.
4. Preserve plain Markdown readability.
5. Run `pnpm run docs:build` for structure, config, or theme changes.
6. Report any standard that could not be followed.

## Verification Checklist

Before a docs change is done, check:

- The page has one visible `#` heading.
- The frontmatter has `title` and `description`.
- Links are descriptive.
- Lists and tables still make sense in GitHub.
- No extra navigation surface was introduced.
- The content says something useful before the visual layer loads.
- Any visual follows the illustration standard and includes useful alt text.
- Any highlighted key term is intentional and not repeated decoratively.

`apps/web/tools/genesis/oauth-providers/` — applied with
`auth-service admin oauth registry set` (#418, #389). Connected providers inject
session env via connection-capability materialization at session start, for
callers that ask for it. Every caller of `buildSessionEnvironment` states a
`ConnectionCredentialPurpose`, and
`buildIntegrationRuntimeEnvironment` withholds every connected-account
credential from a purpose that does not need one. Genesis upkeep runs (memory
consolidation, soul-memory reconciliation) are withheld today and also run
without a shell (TAC-804).

Custom exchange/identity handlers live in `apps/auth/src/handlers/` and ship
with the auth service — not Infra/Ion.

In **Developer mode**, Settings shows a quiet badge per integration for its
credential strategy (`static` or `DCR`) so operators can see deploy requirements
without opening the registry (#473).

Disconnecting or updating an integration clears both the Postgres integration
cache and the in-memory Genesis OAuth registry cache so Settings and the next
session env rebuild stay aligned (#324).

## Connection credential purpose

Connected-account OAuth grants are account-wide. Delivering them into a Hub
session hands the agent every permission the grant carries for the life of that
session. Callers therefore state **why** they need credentials; the delivery
boundary withholds grants from purposes that do not need them (#963, TAC-804).

| Purpose | Delivers credentials | Typical callers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_session` | Yes | Mission, builder, Team, subagent, MCP Host task runs |
| `automation_run` | Yes | Scheduled/triggered automations and Team playbook runs |
| `redaction_only` | Yes (values only) | PII redaction — collected to mask stored text; never reaches an agent shell |
| `system_maintenance` | No | Memory consolidation, soul-memory reconciliation — upkeep without connected-account access |

Implementation: `apps/web/src/domain/connection-credential-purpose.ts`;
`buildIntegrationRuntimeEnvironment` in `integration-runtime-environment.ts`;
every `buildSessionEnvironment` call passes `connectionCredentials`.

When adding a new caller that builds a session environment, pick the narrowest
purpose that matches the work. Do not default to `user_session` for internal
Genesis upkeep.

**Apollo** uses **MCP DCR** instead: Genesis registers an OAuth client against
`mcp.apollo.io`, runs authorize/token directly in-app, and stores tokens in
`user_integration`. No auth-service broker hop and no `GENESIS_APOLLO_*` env vars.

**Printavo** is a **first-party API-key** integration (not broker OAuth). Printavo
GraphQL API v2 authenticates with `email` + `token` headers — there is no OAuth
authorize/token dance. Settings → Connections opens a dialog; Genesis validates
credentials with `account { id }`, stores them encrypted on `user_integration`,
and injects a Printavo row into the Services list (same exception pattern as
Google). Catalog/logo live in `tools/genesis/api-key-providers/printavo.json`.
Collections sync is poll-only (Printavo does not offer HTTPS webhooks). Session
env: `PRINTAVO_EMAIL`, `PRINTAVO_TOKEN`, `PRINTAVO_GRAPHQL_URL`.

Each integration still uses one credential strategy at deploy time:

- Dynamic Client Registration when the service supports it (Apollo, Mercury, Attio, Todoist).
- Environment-provided OAuth client credentials when it does not.
- First-party API-key connect when the vendor has no OAuth (Printavo).

There is no fallback chain. An integration should be clearly configured for one
strategy so agents and operators can reason about deployment requirements.

OAuth callbacks must use the app's public base URL. For local auth cookies, use
the loopback host on port 3500 (see root `AGENTS.md` Cloud agent instructions),
not the `localhost` hostname.

## Google identity provider

Google Workspace is **not** a broker-registry integration. Google is Genesis's
**identity provider** (sign-in) and a **connection capability** at mission
runtime.

| Concern | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Sign-in | `/api/auth/google` → auth service `/genesis/oauth/google/{action}` on `apps/auth` (no `credential_strategy` segment) |
| Connected? | `isGoogleIdentityConnected` — auth-service `getGenesisOAuthToken("google")` succeeds |
| Mission connect card | `/api/auth/google?returnTo=...` — **not** `/api/integrations/google/oauth` |
| Session env | `connection:google` materializes `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_TOKEN` when identity-connected |
| Settings list | Injected when identity-connected even if `google` is absent from the broker registry |

Implementation: `apps/web/src/services/google-identity-integration.ts`.

Agents adding integrations: read
`.agents/skills/genesis-integration/references/google-identity-provider.md`.
Do **not** add `oauth-providers/google.json` unless product explicitly moves
Google onto the broker catalog.

**First Google sign-in bind:** After a cold platform-identity Google login, when
the user has an active tenant org and no durable Workspace grant yet, the auth
callback chains a second org-scoped OAuth hop (`planTenantGoogleWorkspaceBind`)
so Workspace credentials bind to that tenant. Settings and briefing see the
connection without a hard reload.

**Live connection state:** Successful Google connect or disconnect publishes
`integration.connection` over the session-log worker websocket. Settings,
briefing Google surfaces, and TanStack Query caches patch in place via
`query-ws-bridge.ts` — no full-page refresh required (#798).

**Identity subject binding:** Google OAuth tokens are keyed by a durable
**identity subject** (`googleSub` / linked `ionUserId`) in the auth service, not
by ephemeral broker account ids. Sign-in and Workspace reconnect therefore reuse
the same stored grant instead of looping through **Connection Expired** after
every login (#867, #872). Implementation:
`apps/auth/src/google/identity-subject.ts`.

**Scope changes and re-auth:** Settings → **Update access** uses
`googleIdentityConnectUrl({ promptConsent: true, orgId })` so Google re-shows
consent. When Cloud Console scope allowlists change, users may see
`GoogleReauthBanner` until they reconnect with consent (#793, #790).

**New session required:** integration env is built at session start. After Google
re-auth, start a fresh mission session so `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_TOKEN` is present.
`runtime_missing` means the session runtime lacks `gws`, not a stale OAuth state.

**Token refresh:** auth-service coordinates Google refreshes per org, user, and
Google account target with a Redis refresh lock so concurrent callers do not
stampede Google (#1099). Refresh failures carry structured codes such as
`google_refresh_failed` and `google_refresh_invalid_response` for operator logs
(#1097). Implementation: `apps/auth/src/google/token-cache.ts`,
`apps/auth/src/google/flow.ts`.

## MCP Configuration

The `mcp_config` field describes how the app should expose integration tools to
the Hub session environment.

Remote MCP servers are preferred. Local MCP servers are the fallback when a
remote server is unavailable.

During session creation, `buildIntegrationRuntimeEnvironment` materializes
connected integrations into the Hub environment. The session-worker passes
that environment to the assigned Hub process.

## Product Data

Some integrations also contribute direct product context. Integration modules
should return small, structured briefing context rather than large raw payloads.

Current rules:

- wrap module API calls in `try/catch`;
- use shared credential helpers;
- keep context concise;
- separate briefing summary input from action generation input;
- avoid showing the same concrete task twice.

## Settings Surface

Settings → **Connections** (section id `integrations`) lists first-class
Services (broker OAuth), Custom Genesis API keys, and MCP clients. Services
shows connection state, starts OAuth, and lets users disconnect. See
[Connections](connections.md) for the Custom tab and dual-path model.

Connected integrations with **post-connect setup** (for example Salesforce
package install and Hosted MCP enablement) show a **Setup** action on the
integration row and a dedicated subroute at
`/settings/integrations/:integrationId/setup`. Guidance comes from auth-service registry
`runtime_config.post_connect` when present, with app-local fallbacks in
`integration-post-connect.ts` (#605).

Integrations with a **Collections sync module** auto-run **initial sync setup**
after connect (#1050). Genesis enables each adapter's default sync objects and
enqueues the first inbound work on `jobs.integration.sync` (`inbound.setup` /
`inbound.poll`) for `apps/processor` — not on the web request path. Settings →
Integrations → **Settings** shows **Preparing your first sync** until setup
completes. Failures surface **Couldn't start syncing** with entity-specific
copy and a **Retry** action — vendor dumps never appear in the UI. A periodic
job (`integration-sync-poll`) reclaims stale claims, retries infra-not-ready
rows within a one-hour window, and enqueues poll jobs for the processor. Provider
HTTPS webhooks dual-publish to `events.integration` and `jobs.integration.sync`
after a durable inbox write. Local multi-worktree stacks use a per-worktree
Cloudflare quick tunnel (`GENESIS_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`) so providers can reach
the API; see [Collections](collections.md) (Synced collections · Inbound apply
transport) and `pnpm run dev:help`.

Integration logos live on the auth-service OAuth **service** row (`logo` data URI),
applied with `auth-service admin oauth registry set`. Settings renders registry
logos via `registryProviderLogo()` in `integration-icon.tsx`. Do not add new
broker providers to `integration-logos.ts` — bundled assets are legacy fallback
only (#477). Missing logo → generic plug icon.

for preview; Hub sessions use the CLI skill for search, query, and mutations.

Notion OAuth uses brokered Genesis OAuth with `owner=user` on the authorize URL.
Pages and databases must be shared with the Genesis Notion integration before
agents can read or write them.

Jobber OAuth uses brokered Genesis OAuth (auth-service registry). Jobber scopes are
fixed at OAuth-app creation in Jobber's Developer Center, so the authorize URL
sends no scope parameter. Briefing context (clients, requests, quotes, jobs,
visits, invoices) is fetched live from Jobber's GraphQL API via the `jobber`
data module. When a refresh token rotates or expires, Settings disconnect and
reconnect still tear down local sync state and revoke broker credentials even
if the live access token is gone (#746 / TAC-715).

Housecall Pro OAuth uses brokered Genesis OAuth with Ion `handler_kind:
housecallpro` (JSON token exchange/refresh + `GET /company` identity). Genesis
is modeled as a verified Integration Partner — Pros can mint API keys for custom
scripts, but Settings connect does not accept API keys. Redirect URI:
`https://auth.agentcompany.com/genesis/oauth/housecallpro/static/callback`.

## Mission Routing

Broker-connected Settings integrations ship as **connection capabilities**
(`connection:{slug}`) — system-scoped templates in
`packages/connection-capabilities/{slug}/` that hash-sync into the registry at
deploy (#489). When a user connects a provider in Settings, Genesis provisions
the slug's template capability (syncing the system template from
`packages/connection-capabilities/` when the registry row is missing), binds a
broker-addressed connection ref, and materializes tokens at session start through
`buildConnectionCapabilityRuntimeEnvironment` (not a parallel `MCP_SERVERS`
boot path) (#550).

In mission sessions, connected providers appear in
`capability_available_list` like other active capabilities. Lead routes
integration work to executors (typically `generalist`) with the staged
connection-capability `SKILL.md`. Delivery lane matters: CLI/env connections
(Google, Notion, Jobber, QuickBooks, …) use bash/CLI via the skill — they are
**not** `capability_invoke` tool packages. MCP connections (Linear, Slack,
HubSpot, Salesforce, Gusto, Todoist, …) use `mcp_call_tool` per the skill.
Session env still exposes `GENESIS_INTEGRATION_<ID>=available|unavailable`
signals for diagnostics.

Interactive construction surfaces can request `capability_available_list` with
`scope=system` to discover safe system capability summaries, including
disconnected connection templates marked `requires_connection`. The response
contains stable ids, display metadata, and readiness only—never tokens or
delivery configuration. `integration_request` accepts the exact
`connection:{slug}` id (or its returned connection slug), reads the slug from
the template metadata, and confirms the provider still exists in the live broker
before publishing a connect card or URL. Static aliases and prompt examples are
compatibility aids only; they are not action authority.

When the user finishes OAuth and returns to the session with
`?integration_connected=`, the client sends `integration_oauth_connected`
(awaits command ack before stripping the query param). The ack includes
`data.resumed` so optimistic Working chrome clears when resume was deduped
(for example a reload that still has the query param). A sessionStorage
one-shot also skips re-notify after a successful return. If an open connect
card matches, the server resolves it; if the card is already gone, resume
still runs. For mission and automation sessions the server tears down any
warm Hub relay (integration env is built at Hub start), fresh-resumes from
the Pi snapshot, and starts an internal Lead turn so the prior task
continues — the user should not need to re-send the prompt. Team-builder
still auto-completes credential items but does not tear down / auto-resume
Lead. Dismiss does not resume. Resume is deduped per session+integration
(process-local claim + protocol broadcast).

In user-facing replies, Lead names the service and the next step before any
runtime detail. It can say Google is available, Linear is connected but
unavailable in this session, or Notion needs to be connected in Settings. Env
vars, provider slugs, MCP config, and reason codes belong in diagnostics,
review evidence, or implementation discussion.

| User intent | Correct path |
| --- | --- |
| Act through a connected broker provider | Settings OAuth → broker token → connection capability (`connection:{slug}`) staged at session start → executor follows staged skill (CLI/env via bash, or MCP via `mcp_call_tool`) |
| Use org/user-built reusable behavior | User/org registry capability via `capability_invoke` / `capability_available_list` |
| Provider supported but not connected | Discover with `capability_available_list` `scope=system`, then call `integration_request` with the exact registry connection id or slug |
| Missing connection on a tool-backed capability | `capability_invoke` surfaces connection-required chrome; user connects and retries |
| New reusable behavior beyond the provider's normal API | Capability Builder handoff — not a missing integration |

Lead system prompt guidance lives in `packages/agents/agents/lead/agent.md`.
Per-provider template specs:
[Connection Capability Catalog](../../plans/connection-capabilities-catalog.md).
Program status and remaining rollout blocks (CC-6…CC-9):
[Connection Capabilities](../../plans/connection-capabilities-tasks.md).

## Kernel Boundary

Connection capabilities are registry-backed capabilities with broker-resolved
tokens — not ad-hoc session env shortcuts. User-built capabilities still need
explicit registry metadata, tests, evidence, and promotion before mission use.

Do not add new direct token boot paths (`MCP_SERVERS` assembly, ad-hoc pasted
API keys in session env, or per-provider Lead prompt routing) for broker
providers; extend the connection capability catalog and template sync instead.
User-supplied API keys for capabilities belong on Settings → Connections →
Custom via the Gateway secret path.

# Maintaining genesis-expert

Coding agents and humans: keep this packaged agent accurate when product
behavior changes. Mission sessions use it for feature education and routing
(TAC-1026).

## Runtime model (RAG)

- **Soul:** `agent.md` (role, educate-then-hand-off, compact specialist roster).
- **Corpus:** `knowledge/*.md` (rich how-tos; not fully inlined into the prompt).
- **Index:** Postgres `genesis_expert_knowledge` — background materialize on
  deploy/local startup (and lazily on first search when empty). `content_hash`
  gates upsert/re-embed.
- **Rollout lock:** materialize uses Postgres session `pg_try_advisory_lock`
  (`genesis_expert_knowledge_materialize`). One replica loads; peers skip and
  do not block readiness. Startup never awaits materialize.
- **Tools:** `genesis_expert_search`, `genesis_expert_get` (expert-only child surface).

`knowledgeMode: rag` on the agent frontmatter means Hub does **not** append
`knowledge/*.md` into the system prompt.

## When you must update

Update `packages/agents/agents/genesis-expert/` when you:

- Ship a new product surface, route, Settings area, or major feature.
- Change how users perform a routine task (create collection, connect app,
  start a builder, Team flow, automation path).
- Add, rename, enable, or disable a packaged specialist or builder handoff type.
- Change Lead routing, builder handoff catalog, or mission specialist roster.
- Retire a surface or mark a placeholder (for example `/agents`).

Also update product docs under `docs/product/` via `genesis-product-docs`.

After corpus edits ship, background materialize re-indexes changed hashes only.
Local multi-worktree: app start schedules materialize when `DATABASE_URL` is set.
First search also ensures load when the table is still empty (waits briefly if
a peer holds the advisory lock).

## Local test checklist

From `apps/web`:

1. Run `pnpm run dev:help`. Read the slug, `publicOrigin`, and token path.
2. Start or restart with `pnpm run dev:start` or `pnpm run dev:restart` when needed.
3. Confirm materialize in logs: `genesis-expert-knowledge` / `local materialize done`.
4. Confirm rows: `pnpm run dev:sql` then
   `select count(*) filter (where status='active') as active,
           count(*) filter (where embedding is not null and status='active') as emb
    from genesis_expert_knowledge;`
5. Open the worktree `publicOrigin` from `dev:help` (or `runtime.json`). Start a
   mission session. Ask a product how-to (for example App Builder vs Capability
   Builder). Lead hops `genesis-expert` via `subagent_run_*` and calls
   `genesis_expert_search`.
6. Confirm that `Dockerfile.session-worker` copies `packages/` into
   `/opt/genesis/packages`.
   Knowledge markdown does **not** need to ship in the image (RAG is Postgres).
   If the image is stale, rebuild and redeploy the session-worker image.

## What to edit

| Change | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Role / hand-off contract / **compact runtime routing roster** | `agent.md` |
| Feature map / how-tos | `knowledge/*.md` (add freely; prefer section `##` headings for chunks) |
| **Detailed specialist / builder roster** | `knowledge/90-specialists.md` |
| **App Builder** (top-level) | `knowledge/61-app-builder.md` — not only `60-builders.md` |
| Other builders / readiness | `knowledge/60-builders.md` (do not pitch non-GA media builders) |
| **Connectors / outbound MCP** | `knowledge/40-connectors.md` (inbound vs outbound must stay explicit) |
| **MCP Host (inbound clients)** | `knowledge/41-mcp-host.md` |
| **Inboxes (Agent Mail)** | `knowledge/42-agent-mail.md` |
| **Memory** | `knowledge/71-memory.md` |
| **Files** | `knowledge/72-files.md` |
| **Trust / privacy / models / ZDR / sandboxes** | `knowledge/73-trust-privacy-models.md` |
| Settings / access | `knowledge/70-settings-and-access.md` |
| FAQ | `knowledge/95-faq.md` |
| Troubleshooting | `knowledge/96-troubleshooting.md` |
| Specialist / builder roster depth | `knowledge/90-specialists.md` **and** compact table in `agent.md` |
| Schema / search / materialize | `apps/web` product-knowledge services (rare) |

### Production frontmatter (channel gate)

Optional YAML frontmatter at the top of a knowledge file:

```markdown
---
production: false
---

# Draft surface (edge / preview / local only)
```

| `production` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| omitted / `true` | Load everywhere (default). |
| `false` | Load on **edge**, **PR preview**, and **local** only. Skip on customer **stable**. |

Materialize reads `GENESIS_RELEASE_CHANNEL` (then `GENESIS_CHANNEL` /
`GENESIS_DEPLOY_CHANNEL`). Only the bare channel value `stable` is
production-only. Empty channel (local multi-worktree) and values such as
`edge`, `pr-42-edge`, and `pr-12-stable` include draft files.

Use `production: false` for in-progress product education you want on edge
and in local tests before customer stable. Flip to `true` (or remove the
key) when the surface is ready for stable.

Stable materialize retires active rows whose source files drop out of the
scan (including draft files filtered off stable).

**Do not** document Presentations, Meta Ads, or media stubs as generally
available. App Builder may still note `show-apps-builder` + `apps.view` access.

## Checklist (copy into PR notes when relevant)

```text
GENESIS_EXPERT_SYNC:
product_change:
knowledge_files_updated:
production_frontmatter: true|false|n/a
agent_md_roster_updated: yes|no|n/a
specialists_depth_updated: yes|no|n/a
builder_handoff_types_checked: yes|no|n/a
```

## Related sources of truth

- Product behavior: `docs/product/web-app/*.md`
- Lead contract: `docs/product/lead-system-prompt.md`, `packages/agents/agents/lead/agent.md`
- Builder handoff catalog: `apps/web/src/domain/builder-handoff-catalog.ts`
- Materialize / search: `apps/web/src/services/genesis-expert-knowledge.ts`
- Skill for doc drift: `.agents/skills/genesis-product-docs/SKILL.md`

# Connectors (Settings)

Settings → **Connectors** is the product name for access Genesis can use.
Deep links may still use the `integrations` section id.

## Surfaces inside Connectors

| UI area | Purpose | Direction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Catalog** | Built-in apps + public MCP catalog (de-duped) | **Outbound** — Genesis uses these tools |
| **Secrets** | Named encrypted secrets (never paste into chat) | Credentials Genesis stores for outbound use |
| **Genesis** | MCP Host grants for external clients | **Inbound** — clients use Genesis |
| **Activity** | Recent connector / MCP call activity | Both directions (log) |

## Two directions (do not mix)

Genesis supports **both** of these. They are not the same setup path.

| Direction | Plain meaning | Product home | Example intent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Outbound** | Genesis calls an external product or **MCP server** so missions can use its tools | **Catalog** (+ **Secrets** when a key is needed) | “Connect Gmail”, “add this MCP server”, “use Linear in chat” |
| **Inbound** | An external app or coding agent connects **to** Genesis as an MCP client | **Connectors → Genesis** (MCP Host) | “Connect Claude Code / Cursor to Genesis”, “use Genesis from my IDE” |

**How to answer “Can I connect Genesis to Grok / Claude Code?”**

1. **Clarify direction** (or cover both briefly if unclear).
2. **Claude Code / Cursor / similar coding clients → Genesis**  
   Yes, as an **inbound MCP Host** client: Settings → Connectors → **Genesis**.  
   The client talks **to** Genesis (missions, authorized tools). That does **not**
   mean Genesis becomes Claude or Grok, or that all chat history is mirrored.
3. **Genesis → tools from Grok / Claude / some MCP product**  
   Only if that product appears as a **built-in Catalog app** or a **user-managed
   MCP server** Genesis can reach. Do **not** invent a native Connector for Grok
   or Claude Code unless the Catalog shows it. Prefer: check Catalog, or add a
   compatible MCP **server** URL if the user has one.
4. **Never** paste API keys into chat; use Secrets or trusted cards.

A connection only exposes the tools and permissions the user authorizes. It does
not automatically transfer every conversation or guarantee full two-way control.

## Mental model

- **Built-in apps** (Gmail, Calendar, Linear, Slack, GitHub, …) connect through
  Catalog and become usable in sessions when available (**outbound**).
- **User-managed MCP servers** add extra tools Genesis can call (**outbound**).
- **Box** is an experimental built-in outbound app. Its availability depends on workspace rollout and Box permissions.
- **MCP Host (Connectors → Genesis)** lets external clients call **into** Genesis
  (**inbound**). Deep detail: `41-mcp-host`.
- **Secrets** store keys Genesis can bind for outbound auth; users must never
  paste secrets into the chat composer as the primary capture path.
- **Connection required** cards in chat open trusted setup; Settings is the
  durable management surface.
- **Activity** can show inbound client calls and outbound MCP tool calls.

## Mission chat behavior

Lead does **not** run connect/secret/MCP setup tools itself. It hops the
packaged **`integrations`** specialist, which opens trusted cards and returns
status.

After a service is connected and available (**outbound**):

- Domain work (send email, list issues, …) goes to **`generalist`** or the right
  specialist with the staged connection skill / MCP tools.
- If the brief says a connection is **unavailable** in this session runtime,
  explain recovery at product level (reconnect, new session, check Connectors)
  without inventing env var names for the human.

For **inbound** MCP Host setup education, point to Connectors → **Genesis** and
hop **`integrations`** when the human wants the trusted setup flow.

## Common how-tos

### Connect a built-in app (outbound)

1. Settings → Connectors → Catalog, or ask in chat "connect Gmail".
2. Lead hops **`integrations`**; complete the sign-in / consent card.
3. Return to the session and retry the task (a new session can help after connect).

### Connect an IMAP mailbox (outbound, not Google OAuth)

1. Intent: "watch my email" or "trigger when mail arrives" for a generic inbox.
2. Settings → Connectors → Catalog → **Email (IMAP)** (or ask chat to connect IMAP).
3. Enter host, port, TLS, username, and password (Gmail uses an App Password, not
   Google OAuth). Multiple mailboxes are supported.
4. Genesis watches mail through the background processor. You can add an optional
   match rule (plain language) and an optional read-only collection of matching
   mail. Only matching new messages start automations (`imap.message.received`).
   Disconnect and mailbox remove let you keep or delete the email collection.
   This is **not** AgentMail-hosted inboxes and **not** a Collections sync
   adapter.
5. Hop **`integrations`** when a trusted connect card is needed.

### Add an MCP server Genesis can use (outbound)

1. Intent: “Genesis should call tools from this MCP server / product.”
2. Settings → Connectors → **Catalog**, or ask chat to add the product/URL.
3. Prefer catalog search when the product is known; otherwise a direct server URL.
4. Complete OAuth or access-key capture when prompted (Secrets when needed).
5. After save, a **new session** may be needed so runtime picks up tools.

### Connect Claude Code / Cursor / an IDE to Genesis (inbound)

1. Intent: “My coding client should use Genesis (missions / tools).”
2. Settings → Connectors → **Genesis** (MCP Host clients).
3. Authorize the client under product OAuth / grant flow (no keys in chat).
4. In the client, point MCP at Genesis’s MCP Host endpoint as the product UI
   documents — do not invent raw API paths for the human unless they ask for
   diagnostics.
5. Hop **`integrations`** when setup cards or grants need the specialist.

### “Can I connect Grok?”

- **As inbound client (Grok talking to Genesis):** only if that client can act
  as a standard MCP client against MCP Host. Do not promise a branded “Grok
  button” unless Catalog/Genesis UI shows it.
- **As outbound tools (Genesis calling Grok tools):** only via Catalog / MCP
  server if available — not a default native Connector today.
- Prefer honest limits over a long speculative menu.

### Store an API key safely

1. Use Secrets in Connectors (or the trusted capture card in chat).
2. Never paste the key into ordinary chat messages.
3. Secrets are **encrypted at rest**, **partitioned by customer**, and available
   only when the product retrieves them for an authorized use—not as plaintext
   in the transcript. Full privacy framing: trust knowledge
   (`73-trust-privacy-models`).

### “Connected but not working in this session”

1. Do not invent missing custom capabilities first.
2. Explain reconnect, finish OAuth, or start a **new session** so runtime picks
   up the connection.
3. Hop **`integrations`** with the product id when a connect/unavailable card is needed.

### After connect — use the product (outbound)

Connection setup is not the business task. After available:

- Domain work (send email, list issues) → **`generalist`** (or right specialist)
  with the staged connection skill / MCP tools.
- Keep setup cards on **`integrations`**.

## Handoff

| Intent | recommendedNext |
| --- | --- |
| Connect built-in app / outbound MCP / secrets | `specialist` / `integrations` |
| MCP Host / Claude Code / IDE → Genesis | `specialist` / `integrations` (Genesis tab education) |
| Use connected API after available | `specialist` / `generalist` |
| Pure “what is MCP Host vs MCP server?” | Education (`none`) after explaining both |

## Language

Prefer **Connectors**, **connect**, **available / not connected**, **MCP Host**,
**MCP server**, **inbound / outbound** when clarifying direction.
Avoid leading with OAuth, token, MCP JSON, or provider slug dumps unless the
human asked for diagnostics.
Do **not** collapse inbound and outbound into one vague “possible routes” list
without saying which way the connection goes.

# Files

**Files** is the user-wide library for documents and uploads across mounted
drives. Structured business **records** still belong in **Collections**.

## Surfaces

| Surface | Route | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Files browser | `/files` | Browse, search, preview, upload, manage |
| Files help | `/files/help` | Getting started when the library is empty |
| Session attachments | Mission / builder chat | Attach for analysis, import, builder context |
| Generated session files | Session UI | Previews/downloads for files Genesis created |

## Mental model

| | **Files** | **Collections** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shape | Documents, sheets, images, PDFs, folders | Typed rows and fields |
| Browse | `/files` | `/collections` |
| Typical use | Read, attach, upload, preview | Search, update, automate on records |

Drives can include:

- **Genesis** drives (My / company library as product presents them)
- **Google** My Drive / Shared Drives when connected
- Other providers when connected (for example Notion references)

Bytes stay with the owning drive; Genesis indexes metadata for browse/search.

## In sessions

- People **attach** files for analysis, spreadsheet import, and builder context.
- Successful generated paths (reports, PDFs, spoken audio) show as product
  previews or cards. Do **not** tell users to dig a raw sandbox workspace tree.
- Composer and transcript attachment previews use the same preview kinds as Files.

## Common how-tos

### Open the file library

1. Sidebar → **Files** (`/files`).
2. Use All files / Recent / a specific drive / search.

### Upload a file

1. Open `/files` (or empty-state upload / help).
2. Upload into a writable Genesis (or allowed) location.
3. Connect Google first if they expected Drive content and nothing is mounted.

### Attach a file in chat

1. Use the session composer attach control (local and/or Drive as product allows).
2. Ask Genesis what to do (summarize, import to Collection, use in App Builder).

### Import a spreadsheet into Collections

1. Attach the sheet in chat **or** use collection import UI.
2. Prefer Collections create/import paths — not “store the whole sheet in Memory.”

### Preview

1. Open a file in Files or click an attachment in chat.
2. Preview opens in product UI (image, PDF, text, Office kinds as supported).

## Connectors dependency

If Google Drive content is missing:

1. Settings → **Connectors** — connect Google / Workspace as needed.
2. Return to Files; indexing may take a moment after connect.

## Handoff

| Intent | recommendedNext |
| --- | --- |
| Connect Drive / provider | `specialist` / `integrations` |
| Import sheet as business data | Collections how-tos / `builder` collection when creating tables |
| Summarize / analyze a file in chat | `specialist` / `generalist` after attach |
| Browse only | `route` / `/files` |

## Limits

- Files is not the system of record for customers/invoices (use Collections).
- Provider hierarchies do not merge into one fake cross-drive folder tree.
- Do not invent Drive folder IDs or claim uploads succeeded without evidence.
- Presentation **creation** as a full builder is not the same as storing a file
  in Files (and media builders are not prime-time product pitches).

namespace files
    "This namespace contains endpoints and data types for basic file operations."

import async
import common
import file_properties

route search:2 (SearchV2Arg, SearchV2Result, SearchError)
    "Searches for files and folders.
    Note: :route:`search:2` along with :route:`search/continue:2` can only be used to
    retrieve a maximum of 10,000 matches.
    Recent changes may not immediately be reflected in search results due to a short delay in indexing.
    Duplicate results may be returned across pages. Some results may not be returned."

    attrs
        allow_app_folder_app = true
        auth = "user"
        scope = "files.metadata.read"

route search/continue:2 (SearchV2ContinueArg, SearchV2Result, SearchError)
    "Fetches the next page of search results returned from :route:`search:2`.
    Note: :route:`search:2` along with :route:`search/continue:2` can only be used to
    retrieve a maximum of 10,000 matches.
    Recent changes may not immediately be reflected in search results due to a short delay in indexing.
    Duplicate results may be returned across pages. Some results may not be returned."

    attrs
        allow_app_folder_app = true
        auth = "user"
        scope = "files.metadata.read"


alias TagText = String(max_length=32, min_length=1, pattern="[\\w]+")


union Tag
    "Tag that can be added in multiple ways."
    user_generated_tag UserGeneratedTag
        "Tag generated by the user."

    example default
        user_generated_tag = default

union BaseTagError
    path LookupError

union AddTagError extends BaseTagError
    too_many_tags
        "The item already has the maximum supported number of tags."

union RemoveTagError extends BaseTagError
    tag_not_present
        "That tag doesn't exist at this path."

struct UserGeneratedTag
    tag_text TagText

    example default
        tag_text = "my_tag"

struct AddTagArg
    path Path
        "Path to the item to be tagged."
    tag_text TagText
        "The value of the tag to add. Will be automatically converted to lowercase letters."

    example default
        path = "/Prime_Numbers.txt"
        tag_text = "my_tag"

struct RemoveTagArg
    path Path
        "Path to the item to tag."
    tag_text TagText
        "The tag to remove. Will be automatically converted to lowercase letters."

    example default
        path = "/Prime_Numbers.txt"
        tag_text = "my_tag"

struct GetTagsArg
    paths List(Path)
        "Path to the items."

    example default
        paths = ["/Prime_Numbers.txt"]

struct PathToTags

## Warnings (should fix)
- `apps/web/src/services/file-providers/dropbox.ts:316-323` - Dropbox Business roots are not modeled. Mount creation discards `root_info.root_namespace_id` and hard-codes `dropbox-root` at `storage/file-drive.ts:264-274`. Without `Dropbox-API-Path-Root`, `path: ""` targets the member home namespace, not the team root. Persist the namespace root and bind Dropbox requests to it.

- `apps/web/src/services/mounted-cloud-drive-drivers/dropbox.ts:13-20` - The driver validates owner and provider account, but not `drive.orgId === input.orgId`. Every caller must preserve tenant scope. Add the check and a cross-org test; the Box reference carries the same gap.

- `apps/web/src/services/mounted-cloud-drive-drivers/dropbox.ts:51-68` - The driver treats every Dropbox 403 as item loss and marks one index row unavailable. Dropbox also uses 403 for account, team, or feature restrictions. Parse the error tag and transition the mount for mount-level failures.

- `apps/web/src/services/file-providers/dropbox.ts:307-344` - `has_more: true` with no cursor becomes a normal final page. The lazy index then marks omitted children unavailable in `mounted-cloud-drive-file-index.ts:84-107`. Reject that response before index reconciliation and test it.

- `apps/web/src/services/file-providers/dropbox.ts:418` - Both provider layers map every Dropbox item to the account home page. The web mapping repeats this at `web/lib/file-providers.ts:32-37`. Generic PDF and Office previews can display Dropbox home instead of the selected file. Return no native URL, or preserve a provider path that resolves the item.

- `apps/web/src/api/routes/files-next.ts:441-471` - The external DCR trust block is expected. However, the connect button performs a full navigation, and authorize failure returns bare JSON. Redirect to Files with a stable reason and localized trust or allowlist recovery copy.

- `docs/product/web-app/files.md:96-97` - The docs claim that `/dev/ui/file-browser` includes Dropbox. `file-browser-fixtures.ts:153-160` and its test only cover Box. Add a Dropbox drive and file fixture.

- `apps/web/src/api/routes/files-next.ts:434-524` - No route test covers Dropbox state replay, expired state, tenant-bound exchange, callback failure, or safe `returnTo` handling. Adapter tests also omit search nesting, rename, malformed cursors, and 403 classification. The repeatable migration lacks an idempotency and duplicate-active-mount test.

## Suggestions (consider)
- `apps/web/src/services/mounted-drive-hub-tools.ts:31-44,222-236` - Tool descriptions and prompt guidelines name Box only. Use provider-neutral wording or add Dropbox examples.
- `apps/web/tools/genesis/oauth-providers/README.md:18-38` - Add Dropbox to the provider registry inventory.

## Summary
The change cleanly follows the Box broker, mount, schema, attachment, and UI design. The repeatable migration appears idempotent and avoids destructive DDL, but Dropbox namespace and error semantics need stronger handling.

Live Dropbox DCR remains an expected external blocker until trust or allowlisting. No builds or tests ran under the review-only constraint.

content.text:
# OAuth provider registry JSON

One file per service slug: `{slug}.json`. Each file defines the OAuth **service**
row plus one or more nested **connections** (`credential_strategy`, broker
config, `runtime_config`).

Applied to the **Genesis auth service** (`apps/auth`) admin API:

```text
PUT /internal/genesis/oauth/services/:service
GET /internal/genesis/oauth/services/:service
GET /internal/genesis/oauth/services
```

Host: `https://auth.agentcompany.com` (or local `apps/auth` on port 8787).

Auth: HMAC with `AUTH_ADMIN_SECRET` (see `apps/auth/README.md` — signed headers
`X-Genesis-Timestamp` / `X-Genesis-Signature`). There is no `genesis-admin` CLI.

**Logo:** required for new providers — top-level `logo` data URI on the service
row. See `.agents/skills/genesis-integration-oauth-configure/references/logo.md`.

**Redirect URI:** must include `credential_strategy` — e.g.
`https://auth.agentcompany.com/genesis/oauth/salesforce/static/callback`.
**Not** `.../oauth/salesforce/callback`. See
`.agents/skills/genesis-integration-oauth-configure/references/callback-url.md`.

Workflow: `.agents/skills/genesis-integration-oauth-research/` and
`.agents/skills/genesis-integration-oauth-configure/`.

## Providers in this folder

| Slug | Strategy | Category | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agentuity` | static (public client) | developer-tools | App Builder auth |
| `box` | static | productivity | remote MCP |
| `github` | static | developer-tools | remote MCP |
| `linear` | static | project-management | remote MCP |
| `slack` | static | communication | remote MCP |
| `calcom` | static (public client) | scheduling | remote MCP |
| `notion` | static | productivity | session skill |
| `jobber` | static | field-service | native API |
| `housecallpro` | static | field-service | native API |
| `attio` | dcr | crm | remote MCP |
| `salesforce` | static | crm | remote MCP |
| `todoist` | dcr | productivity | remote MCP |
| `mercury` | dcr | finance | remote MCP |
| `gusto` | dcr | finance | remote MCP |
| `wave` | static | finance | native API |
| `quickbooks` | static | finance | native API |
| `xero` | static | finance | native API |
| `sage` | static | finance | native API |

Apply each provider JSON via the auth-service admin `PUT` above (resolve
`${env:VAR}` placeholders in secrets before apply).

Verify catalog (product-signed request) with the auth service integrations
route documented in `apps/auth/README.md`.

## File shape

```json
{
  "name": "GitHub",
  "description": "...",
  "category": "developer-tools",
  "connections": [
    {
      "credential_strategy": "static",
      "lifecycle_status": "experimental",
      "handler_kind": "generic",
      "auth_url": "...",
      "runtime_config": { "mcp_config": { "type": "remote" } }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Env placeholders

Connection string fields may use `${env:GENESIS_SLUG_CLIENT_ID}` style
placeholders. Resolve them in the request body before calling the admin API.
Convention: `GENESIS_{SLUG_UPPER}_CLIENT_ID` and
`GENESIS_{SLUG_UPPER}_CLIENT_SECRET`.

The independent review found no critical issues, but it surfaced several Dropbox-specific edge cases worth fixing before handoff: Business namespace roots, cross-org driver validation, malformed pagination cursors, 403 classification, and misleading native preview links. I’m addressing those now; route-level callback tests remain the main likely follow-up if the current API route harness makes them practical.

content.thinking:
**Reviewing access checks**

I’m thinking about adding a central organization check before the driver. This way, the Box cross-organization test could be updated since it currently only covers user checks. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. linear_prepare_attachment_upload
  Prepare a direct Linear file upload for an existing issue.

Workflow:
1. Call this tool with issue, filename, contentType, and size.
2. Upload raw bytes with PUT to uploadRequest.url outside MCP.
3. All headers in uploadRequest.headers are part of the signed request, so send them verbatim.
4. After PUT succeeds, call create_attachment_from_upload with assetUrl to link it to the issue.

Do not base64-encode or transform the file. Use curl --data-binary @path or fetch(url, { method: 'PUT', body: blob }).
Omitting or modifying any signed header, including casing, will return HTTP 403.
The signed URL must be used within 60 seconds or it will expire.

Upload sequencing:
Prepare, PUT, and finalize one file before calling this tool for another file.
Do not batch multiple prepare_attachment_upload calls before starting the PUTs because earlier signed URLs can expire while later files are prepared.

Example:
curl -X PUT --data-binary @file.png \
  -H "content-type: image/png" \
  -H "x-goog-content-length-range: N,N" \
  -H "cache-control: public, max-age=31536000" \
  -H 'Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="file.png"' \
  "<uploadRequest.url>"

Validation:
- auth: 113 tests passed + typecheck
- focused web coverage: 107 tests passed + typecheck
- Biome, generated-schema check, and schema/migration-pair check passed

Not applied or run: OAuth registry apply, `db:migrate`, production changes, or live OAuth E2E. Live DCR remains blocked until Dropbox trusts/allowlists Genesis as a DCR client.
